itens.readme:
# Pi Bot
**An open-source, local-first AI agent team for your desktop.** Named AI Bots work on your own
computer: chat with one or put several in a group chat, and they plan, run commands, edit files,
browse the web and use your computer, while every risky step waits for your approval. Runs on
macOS, Windows and Linux, with an Android app. Built on the [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
agent kernel.
 ▶  Watch the 60-second video  ·  Download  ·  User guide  ·  Online docs  
[English](README.md) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md)
Pi Bot is a desktop app in which a team of named Bots works on your own computer. You chat with a
Bot directly or put several in a group chat, give them a working folder, and they plan, run
commands, edit files and hand work to each other, while every risky step waits for your approval.
The "brain" runs on your machine too: chats, files, memory and keys stay local, and only the
model provider you choose sees the prompts you send.
Website and downloads:   · User guide: [docs/guide](docs/guide/README.md) · Online docs:  
## What it does
- **Bots and roles.** Create Bots with a name, a role (developer, researcher, writer, translator,
  …), their own model, skills, permissions and memory.
- **Direct and group chats.** A group has a coordinator that plans, hands steps to members and
  collects the results; you confirm the plan before it runs.
- **Working folders and changes.** Bots work inside folders you choose. Every change is listed,

# Agentic Attack Detections
[ ](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/actions/workflows/validate.yml)
[ ](https://github.com/ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections/releases)
[ ](LICENSE)
Open-source detection rules, hunting queries and indicators for security teams. They cover agentic attack frameworks: tools that hand an intrusion to AI agents, which plan, run real attack tools and keep going until they reach a goal.
Free to use under the MIT license. Fixes, false-positive reports and new indicators are welcome.
## What is here
- **Framework folders.** ARTEX and its AntiFox fork, Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, CyberStrikeAI, Strix, Hermes Agent, Agent Zero, RedAmon, Xalgorix and Pentest Swarm AI. Each folder is built from a review of the framework's source code and the public reporting on its use.
- **Shared behaviors.** Rules for what these frameworks have in common, whatever the tool or the model behind it.
- **Indicators and feeds.** One CSV of 572 sourced indicators, and the feeds generated from it.
- **Exposed consoles.** A dated list of addresses where one of these consoles answers on the internet, in [`exposure/`](exposure), with a [count per framework](#exposed-consoles). It is a record of what is exposed, not a detection feed.
Formats: KQL for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR, Sigma, Suricata, Zeek, YARA and STIX 2.1, plus WAF rules for Cloudflare, AWS WAF and Azure WAF. Splunk and Elastic are covered by a Splunk app and Elastic rules for ARTEX,

**antislop** is a rulebook an AI coding agent reads every session. It stops generic UI, text, and AI-shaped code, and it is a filter, not a style guide: no colors, fonts, or layouts prescribed, direction stays yours. Inside are 40 rules in three tiers, a Liveliness Toolkit, a mandatory PASS/FAIL report, and six skills that load only when a task needs them. It cannot invent direction, so DESIGN.md supplies that, and antislop never beautifies on its own.
## Before and after
Each pair below is one brief, run twice, so the difference is visible side by side.
### UI
With /antislop-ui. antislop alone is not the after. It removes the slop and stops there; direction comes from `DESIGN.md`. For UI work you intend to ship, that file is mandatory: without it the result is labelled a draft without direction. The pair below is the result.
| **Before: without antislop** | **After: antislop + `DESIGN.md`** |
|:--|:--|
|     |     |
| This is what most AI output looks like: slop everywhere once you take a closer look. | Much better. antislop kills the slop, and `DESIGN.md` gives it a real visual direction. |

itens.descricao_en: Long-term memory runtime for AI agents — plain Markdown as the source of truth, local ranked retrieval, and an independent sleep-time Manage layer. Claude Code and Codex share one store. No API key.
itens.readme:
### agent-memory: the long-term memory runtime for AI agents
 Invariants  ·  Skill  ·  Issues 
***
An agent that closes its session forgets everything it learned in it. agent-memory is the
runtime that fixes that, for any agent — not only coding ones. Markdown files in one store are
the single source of truth, the SQLite index beside them is a cache you can delete at any time,
and Claude Code, Codex CLI, Muse Code, and anything else that can run a shell command share
that store.
Retrieval is local and ranked, and it answers with paths rather than pasted text — the agent
opens each hit only as deep as the task needs. Writes do not wait for the agent to remember to
make them: they fire at conversation boundaries. A sleep-time pass then consolidates and
forgets by value, on its own clock. None of it needs an API key.
## Two lines, one store
Agent memory has grown along two architectural lines. One builds a **retrieval engine** —
embeddings, a knowledge graph, a ranking pipeline — which finds the right thing, but hands the
agent an opaque chunk it cannot inspect and a store it cannot migrate off. The other hands the
agent a **filesystem** — markdown it reads directly, browsable with `ls` and `grep` — which is
legible and costs nothing to run, but does not rank, and stops scaling the moment the tree
outgrows a listing.
